correctness.rationale: Energy H=exp(beta*x^2)*y^2/2+int_0^x s(1+alpha*s^2)exp(beta*s^2) ds has exact zero derivative. Every positive energy level is one regular compact oval. The unchanged-time coordinate q=int_0^x exp(beta*s^2/2)ds has force derivative h'(q)=1+(beta+3alpha)x^2+alpha*beta*x^4, so h(q)/q strictly increases, implying strict period decrease. The exact turning-variable density K_A has J_A/m=int_0^s(1-cu)e^-u du, 0<=c<=1/B. On s<=B/2, K_A<=2K; on s>=B/2, its total contribution is O(B exp(-B/4)), uniformly in alpha. Since int K=pi, the period constant and L1/total-variation law follow for all alpha(A)>=0. Standalone checker passed from the package; finite tests do not replace the analytic proof. Boundary beta>0 fixed and all amplitude quantifiers were checked.

value.rationale: This is the natural entire two-parameter global-center subfamily where velocity-squared feedback and cubic restoring stiffness compete. It yields a strict full-amplitude period classification and sharp noncommuting scaling transition: fixed zero restoring term gives T of order A^-1, fixed positive restoring term T of order A^-2, while alpha=c/A^2 has a nontrivial exact crossover constant. The original-time Beta(1/2,1/2) turning-deficit distribution is a new precise, robust occupation invariant that survives every nonnegative restoring coefficient. The combination addresses global period dynamics and localized high-energy statistics, not a routine renaming, arbitrary finite slice or known-table recomputation.
